newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T extends loss, results seen at low end.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T extends loss, results seen at low end.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc extended earlier losses after full-year profits which fell short of analyst expectations and the stock succumbed to profit-taking after recent gains, traders said.
There was also some disappointment that the company had said nothing about a demerger of its tobacco and insurance arms, long the subject of market speculation.

"The pre-tax profit figure looked a bit light and there was no news on a potential demerger," said one senior trader. Added another: "The results were a tad disappointing and having had a good run I'm not surprised to see the stock coming off."
B.A.T shares, up 32 percent since early last November, were down 19-1/2p at 530 by 0936 GMT in active trade of 5.5 million shares.
Pre-tax profit from the group rose five percent to 2.495 billion stg, after a charge of 160 million charge to cover U.S. environmental claims at its insurance unit Eagle Star.

The company also doused hopes for a U.S. legal settlement on tobacco-related disease claims, which helped drive the recent rally in its shares, saying the U.S. tobacco industry has no intention of proposing a settlement. It added that it believed it had no liability from any claims.
